headline: A one-team state that worships 1990s grit, buys for big families and dresses for the canyon, not the club.
thesis: The Jazz are the only NBA team for the whole Wasatch Front and beyond, from Ogden and Logan to Provo, St. George, southern Idaho and Wyoming, and they share the Delta Center and its team store with the NHL's Utah Mammoth under Smith Entertainment Group. Volume is statewide, family-sized and kids-first, while taste is set by a thin layer: Sugar House and Granary District all-ages DIY culture, and the West Side's Pacific Islander and Latino families, for whom church-ward, rec and high school basketball sit beside football. Fans hold the Stockton-Malone-Sloan era as a moral standard, a younger cohort grew up on the Mitchell-Gobert playoff years, and everyone treats technical outdoor layers as everyday clothes. The gray-gradient City Edition repeats and the Jazz are off the opening-night, Christmas and Specter stages, so this is a local year. Nike wins by turning the gray gradient into Utah material (inversion haze, granite, salt crust) in its own cold-weather layers, building a Peterson-and-Bailey youth program in the current purple, black and sky blue, and using the year to earn West Side and DIY credibility ahead of a place-rooted future City Edition.

archetype.name: The Statewide Family Loyalist
archetype.description: A fan who drives in on I-15 with three kids in purple youth jerseys, measures every new star against Stockton and Malone, and arrives in a puffer and beanie because the January walk to the Delta Center is cold. Loyal to the team over any brand, patient with a rebuild but allergic to hype.

pulse.teamMoment: Coming off 22-60, Utah speeds up its youth movement with No. 2 pick Darryn Peterson and Ace Bailey beside Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. Will Hardy is under pressure to develop them, and BetMGM's 35.5-win total asks for about 13 more wins.
pulse.sentiment: Impatient but curious: tired after a bottom-of-the-league year, energized by Peterson and the Jackson Jr. trade, and expecting visible progress and a play-in chase rather than a playoff run.

topInsights.title: The repeat City Edition needs a material story, not a relaunch
topInsights.insight: The vertical gray gradient with baby blue trim is on court for a second straight season, so there is no debut spike to sell. Every lens maps that gray onto something locals live with: the winter inversion haze, Wasatch granite, the salt crust of the Bonneville flats and a clear high-desert sky after a storm.
topInsights.implication: Refresh the gradient through textures and outerwear (salt-crackle print, granite-speckle fleece, inversion-to-sky fades) and never market it as new; save the big story for the next City Edition.

topInsights.title: Buy for five kids, not one collector
topInsights.insight: Utah has the largest average household and the youngest median age of any state, and Jazz purchases are made in multiples on a once-a-season family trip to the Delta Center, a Murray or Orem mall, or Dick's. Deseret Industries thrifting and value-tier buying are normal, and authentic jerseys are a small collector niche.
topInsights.implication: Lead with deep youth and toddler sizing in the current Mountain Purple, black and sky blue palette, matching kid-to-adult sets and bundle-friendly entry tees; keep premium to a small, clearly separated tier.

topInsights.title: Canyon wardrobe is game-night wardrobe
topInsights.insight: Locals ski Alta, Snowbird and Brighton after work, hoop in cold church and rec-center gyms all winter, and wear technical outdoor shells, fleece and snap-pocket layers as everyday clothes. Puffers, fleece and beanies are what fans wear to the Delta Center from November through March.
topInsights.implication: Make outerwear and layering the core of the Jazz assortment inside Nike's own ACG and NBA outerwear lanes, borrowing local technical codes (shell cuts, snap pockets, drawcords) rather than partnering with outdoor competitors.

topInsights.title: Three eras, and an origin that is known but never designed
topInsights.insight: Fans divide into Note-era (1979-96) and 1996 Mountain-era loyalists, both thrifted at DI and cut up by younger fans, while fans now in their 20s grew up on the 2017-22 Donovan Mitchell and Rudy Gobert playoff teams. Everyone knows the 'no jazz in Utah' joke and the New Orleans start, but no product tells it well.
topInsights.implication: Run separate era capsules rather than mixing palettes, add a Mitchell-Gobert bridge chapter to Peterson, and put the New Orleans origin on labels and inserts with the team mark, not a player name. Confirm which licensee holds heritage jerseys first.

topInsights.title: The West Side plays hard and is barely served
topInsights.insight: Rose Park, Glendale, West Valley and Kearns hold one of the highest per-capita Pacific Islander populations in the US plus large Latino communities, and they are a major part of the valley's youth basketball and football, from church-ward leagues to high school programs. They have few premium doors and appear on almost no Jazz product.
topInsights.implication: Co-create a capsule with paid, credited Tongan, Samoan and Latino designers, each community with its own credit and approval rights, using PIK2AR and Centro Civico Mexicano for cultural review and access, not as design studios. Never lift tatau, tapa or ceremonial patterns.

topInsights.title: Utah taste grew up all-ages
topInsights.insight: With a young population and few under-21 rooms elsewhere, the scene was built in all-ages venues like Kilby Court and documented by SLUG Magazine, whose screen-printed flyers and Gallery Stroll openings are the local graphic language.
topInsights.implication: Use gig-poster screen prints, hand-lettered date blocks and cassette and 7-inch packaging as the lifestyle graphic language in Jazz purple, black and sky blue inks; keep bar imagery and jokes about the state's religious culture off the line.

topInsights.title: A calendar with local quiet zones and no national stage
topInsights.insight: General Conference empties the first weekends of April and October, many households keep Sunday as a family day, Halloween is a major neighborhood night, and July 24 Pioneer Day outranks any summer NBA date. The Jazz are on neither the opening-night nor the Christmas slate.
topInsights.implication: Stage in-person drops on Fridays and Saturdays around confirmed home dates, avoid Oct 31, push Sunday demand to digital, and plan December as local family gifting rather than a national TV moment.

collection.name: Wasatch Front
collection.story: A collection built from the strip of land every Jazz fan shares: snow and granite above, salt and lake below, and gyms, all-ages rooms and family courts in between. It makes the gray City Edition feel like Utah, honors the two eras fans already love, and hands the West Side and DIY scenes the pen.

themes.name: Inversion Layer
themes.story: The winter haze that traps the valley, then the clear blue sky after a storm, turned into the gradient fans see on court. Built for the canyon commute and the cold walk into the arena.
themes.graphics: Vertical gray-to-sky fades, granite-speckle and salt-crackle tonal prints, and a single-line Wasatch ridgeline on hems and liners.
themes.materials: Quilted water-repellent nylon, heavyweight brushed fleece, ripstop shells with snap utility pockets, and baby-blue drawcords and cuffs.

pieces.detail: Charcoal-to-gray baffle fade with a baby-blue zipper pull and a ridgeline-printed liner.
Oversized ripstop shell with a tonal salt-crust print and snap pockets for gym-to-street wear.
Speckled heavyweight fleece with a grid-coordinate sleeve hit in clean sans numerals.
Gray knit with a baby-blue tipped cuff and a small woven Jazz tab.
The same fade in youth and toddler sizes, sold as a set with the adult hoodie.

themes.name: Note, Mountain and Playoff Years
themes.story: The eras Utah argues about, kept apart and treated with respect: the Note years that carried the New Orleans colors, the 1996 Finals-era Mountain, and the Mitchell-Gobert playoff run a younger generation grew up on.
themes.segment: Heritage diehards, fans in their 20s and parents buying for kids
themes.graphics: Licensed original Note and 1996 Mountain marks, never redrawn, with vintage-wash and cracked-ink finishes that echo DI thrift finds; the New Orleans origin told on neck labels and inserts.
themes.materials: Garment-dyed slub jersey, loopback French terry, tricot warm-ups with snap sleeves, and chain-stitch embroidery.

pieces.detail: Faded purple with the original Note mark and a printed New Orleans 1974 origin neck label.
Tricot warm-up with the 1996 ridgeline in teal and copper piping, licensed through the team.
2017-22 era team marks with a season-by-season playoff date block; no player names unless licensed.
Chain-stitched Note over a gold-and-green rib trim.

themes.name: All-Ages
themes.story: Utah's taste grew up in all-ages rooms, not bars. This theme speaks that language through the gig-poster and flyer culture of Kilby Court, SLUG and Gallery Stroll.
themes.segment: Gen Z fans, the Sugar House and Granary creative crowd
themes.graphics: Two- and three-color off-register screen prints, hand-lettered date blocks for each home month, and cassette and 7-inch sleeve layouts.
themes.materials: Locally screen-printed heavyweight cotton, garment dye, water-based inks, and recycled-board sleeve packaging.

pieces.detail: A different commissioned Utah artist each month, numbered run, artist credited on the hem.
Garment-dyed tee with a cracked-ink 'All-Ages' Jazz lockup.
Record-sleeve packaging with a local-artist playlist QR.
Three pairs in purple, black and sky with a halftone flyer-dot knit.

themes.name: West Side Courts
themes.story: The church gyms, rec centers and family courts of Rose Park, Glendale, West Valley and Kearns, designed by the people who play there.
themes.segment: Pacific Islander and Latino basketball families on the West Side
themes.graphics: Set entirely by paid, credited community designers, with Tongan, Samoan and Latino designers each holding credit and approval over their own pieces; Nike provides the canvas, not the motifs. No tatau, tapa or ceremonial patterns unless the collaborators and their communities choose and approve them.
themes.materials: Durable mesh practice fabrics, heavyweight fleece and family-size runs from youth XS to adult 4XL.

pieces.detail: Reversible mesh with the designer's name and neighborhood on the jock tag.
Long-sleeve shooter with a collaborator-led chest graphic.
Kids' sizes priced for big families, with a share of proceeds to West Side rec leagues.
Outdoor ball with the collaborator's artwork, gifted to local rec programs.

uniform.narrative: The state's namesake lake is shrinking, and its salt crust, shoreline contours and Bonneville land-speed culture are shared Utah icons. A dark shale City Edition with tonal shoreline contours, salt-white numerals and land-speed lettering tells a story only Utah can wear, keeps clear of the white Association uniform, and anchors in the franchise's Mountain Purple. It is a proposal needing Nike NBA uniform, team and league sign-off, realistically for 2028-29 if 2027-28 is already locked.
motifs: Tonal shoreline contour lines across a shale body, drawn from Great Salt Lake topography rather than any artwork
Salt-crust crackle texture in the side panels
Hand-painted land-speed numerals and pinstriping from Bonneville Speed Week culture
A single Wasatch ridgeline at the hem, the mountains seen from the lake
uniform.typography: Custom numerals in the style of hand-painted land-speed race numbers, salt white with a thin purple pinstripe outline; a clean sans wordmark with grid-coordinate styling.
details: Jock tag set in Salt Lake grid-coordinate typography, the way locals give directions
North Arm Pink limited to a thin waistband or neck-tape line, and only if fan testing supports it
Neck tape carrying a single ridgeline-to-shoreline line
Court tie-in: a shale baseline band with salt-white shoreline contours
Any lake commitment made through a nonpartisan, science-based Great Salt Lake partner chosen early with the team
avoid: A white or salt-white base that reads like the Association uniform
Repeating the vertical gray gradient or baby-blue trim as the lead story
Replicating Spiral Jetty or any Smithson-derived spiral without Holt-Smithson Foundation engagement
Temple, Temple Square, pioneer-trek or any Latter-day Saint sacred imagery, and Pacific Islander or Native ceremonial patterns
Utah red, BYU blue or Utah State navy, Olympic marks and Utah Mammoth cues that blur team identity

alternates.name: Mardi Gras to the Wasatch
alternates.idea: A purple, gold and green uniform telling the 1974 New Orleans origin and the 1979 move, built with a credited New Orleans-side designer so it reads as heritage, not costume.

alternates.name: West Side Courts

alternates.name: Speed Week
alternates.idea: A shale and chrome uniform built around Bonneville land-speed numerals and pinstripes, a Utah-only hot-rod language.

partners.name: Pacific Islander Knowledge 2 Action Resources (PIK2AR)
partners.why: A credible Utah Pacific Islander health, education and advocacy organization, trusted by Tongan and Samoan families on the West Side.
partners.idea: Paid cultural-review and community-access partner for the West Side Court Collective, with proceeds to youth rec; not the design studio.

partners.name: Centro Civico Mexicano
partners.why: A decades-old West Side Latino civic and cultural hub with its own events calendar.
partners.idea: Cultural review for Latino pieces and a sales and launch venue at its community events.

partners.name: Mestizo Institute of Culture and Arts (confirm)
partners.why: A West Side Latino arts organization that could connect the capsule to working Latino designers.
partners.idea: Co-recruit and pay Latino designers for the capsule and the September drop.

partners.name: Salt Lake Arts Council (Living Traditions Festival)
partners.why: Runs Living Traditions and public-art programs that reach Pacific Islander, Latino and other community artists.
partners.idea: Designer recruitment through its artist networks and the May reveal at Living Traditions, with the artists on site.

partners.name: Craft Lake City
partners.why: Runs the state's busiest maker marketplace and can introduce vetted screen printers and designers.
partners.idea: Curate the monthly Delta Night poster artists and printers, and use DIY Fest to scout the next season.

partners.name: Kilby Court
partners.why: The emotional center of Utah's all-ages DIY scene and where young taste is set.
partners.idea: Sell each month's poster tee at a Kilby show the week of release, with the poster artist doing the night's flyer.

partners.name: SLUG Magazine
partners.why: Has documented Salt Lake Under Ground for decades; its poster culture is the graphic reference.
partners.idea: Editorial partner for the poster series: artist profiles and a printed season-set zine.

partners.name: Salt Lake City Stars
partners.why: Lower-priced games that reach families who rarely get to the Delta Center.
partners.idea: A family-priced youth table and prospect tees at Stars home games.

where: Delta Center team store as the game-night volume engine (shared with Utah Mammoth product), with City Creek catching pre-game foot traffic
Suburban volume doors along I-15: Fashion Place in Murray, University Place in Orem, Provo Towne Centre and Dick's, deep in youth sizes
Sugar House, Kilby Court and Gallery Stroll for limited taste-setting drops
West Side community events (Centro Civico Mexicano, Sorenson Unity Center) and a named West Valley door to confirm
Salt Lake City Stars games and Saturday I-15 pop-ups as entry-price doors; Park City last, for visitor outerwear
when: Oct 12 to Dec 24 is the season: launch before the first home game, peak at Black Friday and close on family gifting
Mid-November ski openings through March for the cold-weather line
Fridays and Saturdays for in-person drops; Sundays, Halloween and General Conference weekends go digital only
Late June draft and July Summer League (2027 dates not yet announced) as the offseason spikes
how: Good-better-best structure with a visible entry tier, bundle pricing and matching kid-to-adult sets
Separate era capsules (Note, Mountain, playoff years, City Edition, current) so each fan sees their own team
Small, numbered, locally printed runs for scarcity in a market with few boutiques
Pay and credit West Side and DIY collaborators on product, and route proceeds to youth rec
Keep Jazz merchandising visibly distinct from Utah Mammoth and college colors in the shared arena store

risks.risk: Wrong core colors: earlier dossiers described navy and yellow, but the current rotation is a white Association, purple Icon and black Statement in Mountain Purple, Midnight Black and Sky Blue.
risks.mitigation: Ship youth and core product in purple, black and sky blue only, and confirm the exact 2026-27 hexes with the team before colorways lock.

risks.risk: City Edition fatigue in a second season of the same gray gradient.
risks.mitigation: Sell it as material and outerwear, never as new, and announce the next City Edition direction early.

risks.risk: Cultural missteps with Pacific Islander, Latino, Native or Latter-day Saint imagery, or with the state's religious culture as a punchline.
risks.mitigation: Co-create only with paid, credited designers, give each community its own approval, keep church and temple imagery and drink or diet jokes out, and run cultural review before sampling.

risks.risk: Licensing gaps on heritage jerseys and marks, Stockton, Malone, Sloan, Maravich and Mitchell names, and Smithson-derived imagery.
risks.mitigation: Confirm the heritage-jersey licensee, clear team, NBA, NBPA and estate rights first, and use team marks and unbranded cues (salt texture, ridgelines) where rights are uncertain.

risks.risk: Rebuild volatility: a slow start or deadline move can swing demand between Peterson, Bailey, Markkanen and Jackson Jr.
risks.mitigation: Hold player-specific depth on youth tees and fast-print capacity, and re-weight after the first month and at the Feb 11 deadline.

scorecard.rationale: A small metro but a whole-state, family-sized, youth-heavy buyer base with deep one-team loyalty and an unusually distinct design vocabulary (salt, snow, all-ages DIY, West Side hoops). Retail is dispersed along I-15 with a thin boutique layer, and a rebuild year with no national stage caps the near-term upside.
